rule: rust-async-background-work checklist #22: "Does every long-running loop have a defined exit?" — a transient IO error is not one; the daemon must degrade, not stop.
summary: Any error returned by `UnixListener::accept` — including the transient `ECONNABORTED`, `EMFILE` and `ENFILE` — breaks the accept loop, and `main` propagates that error out of `main`, terminating `fleetd` and every PTY it hosts.
failure_scenario: The daemon has several terminals open (each `Pty` holds a master fd, a cloned reader fd, and the child's fds) plus job log files and per-host remote links, and reaches the process fd limit. The next `accept()` returns `EMFILE`. Instead of logging and continuing — after which closing one terminal would restore service — the loop breaks, `main` returns `Err`, and the process exits. Every `TerminalOwner` thread dies with the process, so all the user's running shells and agents are killed by a recoverable resource hiccup. `ECONNABORTED` (a client that connected and reset before `accept` returned) reproduces the same shutdown with no resource pressure at all.
proposed_fix: Classify the error: `if is_fatal_accept_error(&error) { break Err(DaemonError::fs(&self.socket_path, error)) }` and otherwise `tracing::warn!(%error, "transient accept failure"); continue;`. Treat `ECONNABORTED`, `EINTR`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, `ENOBUFS`, `ENOMEM`, `EPERM` as transient (add a short `tokio::time::sleep` back-off for the `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` pair so the loop does not spin on a backlog entry it cannot accept), and only `EBADF`/`EINVAL`/`ENOTSOCK` — a listener that can never work again — as fatal.
test_plan: Add `fn accept_error_is_fatal(error: &std::io::Error) -> bool` next to `try_admit` and a `#[test] fn transient_accept_errors_do_not_stop_the_listener()` in `server/listener.rs`'s test module asserting `!accept_error_is_fatal(&io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::ECONNABORTED))`, `!…(libc::EMFILE)`, `!…(libc::EINTR)` and `accept_error_is_fatal(&io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::EBADF))`. The test cannot compile before the fix because the classifier does not exist, and the current loop's unconditional `break Err(..)` is exactly what it forces to change.
verify_reason: Verified verbatim. crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/listener.rs:187-191 breaks the accept loop with `break Err(DaemonError::fs(&self.socket_path, error))` for any `accept()` error, with no classification. That value becomes `result` (listener.rs:184/:226) and main.rs:104-107 does `let result = listener.run().await; shutdown.cancel(); periodic.join().await; result?;` — so the process exits and every terminal/PTY the daemon hosts dies with it. The contrast the finding draws is accurate: the very next arm (listener.rs:192-196) logs and `continue`s for the connection-limit case. `ECONNABORTED` and `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` are ordinary transient outcomes of `accept(2)`, and the daemon is exactly the process that accumulates fds (PTY master + reader clone per terminal, job log handles, per-host remote links), so EMFILE is reachable without any external attacker.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/listener.rs (accept arm + a new classifier and its unit test). No change to main.rs is required — the fatal path still returns Err. Socket/pid cleanup is unaffected (it rides on `_singleton`). Any test asserting that a broken listener terminates `run()` would need to use a fatal errno.
corrected_fix: Broadly as proposed, with two adjustments: drop EPERM from the transient set (it is a TCP/firewall condition, not a Unix-socket one, and silently looping on it hides a real misconfiguration), and make the EMFILE/ENFILE back-off mandatory rather than optional — those errors leave the connection in the backlog, so a bare `continue` busy-spins a runtime thread. Use a short capped back-off (e.g. 100 ms, and log at warn once per burst rather than per iteration so an fd exhaustion does not flood the log). Keep EBADF/EINVAL/ENOTSOCK fatal.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 12 / checklist #24: "Does a `tokio::select!` with a shutdown or control branch use `biased;` with that branch first?" — "no" means fix before merge.
summary: Every `tokio::select!` in the server with a `shutdown.cancelled()` branch omits `biased;`, so once shutdown is requested the control branch competes at random against permanently-ready data branches instead of winning deterministically.
evidence: There is not one `biased;` anywhere in the workspace (`grep -rn "biased" crates/` returns nothing). The four affected loops are `crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:142-143` (`tokio::select! {` / `() = self.shutdown.cancelled() => break Ok(()),` — competing with five hot branches: `&mut writer`, `reader.next()`, `pending.next()`, `events.recv()`, `frames.recv()`), `server/listener.rs:185-186` (accept loop), `server/listener.rs:249-250` (job forwarder), and `server/listener.rs:297-298` (session forwarder). The skill names `crates/fleet-client/src/terminal.rs:271-274` as the shape to copy.
failure_scenario: A client sends `DaemonShutdown`; connection.rs:255 calls `self.shutdown.cancel()`, which every other connection actor must observe. In a session with an attached terminal producing 60 frames/s plus a streaming agent publishing an event per 16 ms tick, `frames.recv()` and `events.recv()` are ready on essentially every poll, so `shutdown.cancelled()` — although ready and listed first — is chosen with probability 1/6 per iteration. Each losing iteration forwards one more frame or event to a client that has already been told the daemon is going away, and the exact number is seed-dependent, which is precisely what makes an ordering assertion untestable today. The same non-determinism means the listener can accept and fully handshake a brand-new client after `shutdown.cancel()` (listener.rs:187-203), which then gets aborted mid-request by `connections.abort_all()` (listener.rs:221).
proposed_fix: Add `biased;` as the first line of each of the four `tokio::select!` blocks, keeping the `shutdown.cancelled()` arm first, exactly as the skill's daemon pattern shows.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test(flavor = "current_thread")] async fn shutdown_wins_over_a_saturated_event_stream()` to `server/connection.rs`'s test module: run a `Connection` actor subscribed to `EventKind::Toast`, spawn a publisher that pushes a `Event::Toast` and `yield_now().await` in a loop, record the client's received-event count, call `shutdown.cancel()`, await the actor, and assert **zero** further events were written after the cancel. With `biased;` the first poll after cancellation always takes the shutdown arm, so the assertion holds; today it fails for most interleavings.
verify_reason: The convention is stated by the project's own skill, and the code violates it. .claude/skills/rust-async-background-work/SKILL.md:112-113 ('fleetd has 40 `tokio::select!` and **zero** `biased;`, so today shutdown races output on every one'), the anti-pattern table at SKILL.md:268, the daemon pattern at SKILL.md:223-239, and checklist item 24 (references/checklist.md:127-129). `grep -rn biased crates/` returns nothing, and the four cited sites are real: server/connection.rs:142-143, server/listener.rs:185-186, listener.rs:249-250, listener.rs:297-298 — all with `() = shutdown.cancelled() => ...` as an unbiased arm. One evidence error: fleet-client/src/terminal.rs:271-274 is cited as 'the shape to copy' but that select has no `biased;` either (it is a two-arm `updates.closed()`/`events.recv()` select); the actual reference shape is SKILL.md:229.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/listener.rs (3 selects) and crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs (1 select, 6 arms). Adding `biased;` to connection.rs changes polling order for every request, so the existing connection tests (connection.rs test module, incl. event_lag_forces_reconnect_and_full_frames and the serialized-terminal-request harness at connection.rs:222-233) should be re-run for ordering sensitivity.
corrected_fix: Apply the blanket `biased;` only to the three simple loops (listener.rs:185, :249, :297) where the arms are shutdown + one work source. For connection.rs:142 do not blanket-bias the 6-arm select: `biased;` is all-or-nothing, and with the arms in their current order a client that keeps `reader.next()` perpetually ready would starve `events.recv()` and `frames.recv()`, manufacturing exactly the broadcast lag that connection.rs:276-310 has to recover from. Either add `biased;` and reorder deliberately (shutdown, writer join, then the channel arms, with the reader last so it cannot starve the buses), or leave the select fair and break early on `self.shutdown.is_cancelled()` at the top of each iteration. Either way the fix must be justified per-site, not applied mechanically to all 40 selects.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it"; rust-async-background-work checklist #17 and "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places".
summary: The broadcast-lag recovery path discards the result of every `RequestFullFrame` dispatch with `let _ignored`, while the disconnect-cleanup path a few lines away classifies the identical dispatch result and logs anything that is not `NotFound` — so a failed resync leaves the client's terminal grid permanently stale with no trace.
failure_scenario: A client stalls, the shared event bus laps it, and the `Lagged` arm fires. `request_full_frames` dispatches `RequestFullFrame` for each attached terminal; the terminal host's bounded command queue rejects it with `HostError::QueueFull` (fleet-term/src/host.rs:143-154, reached from `send_command`/`reserve_command_bytes`, host.rs:343-384) — the same backlog condition that caused the lag in the first place. The error is dropped, no retry is scheduled and nothing is logged, so the client keeps applying dirty-row diffs onto a grid that is missing rows: a visibly corrupted terminal that only heals on the next attach or resize, with no daemon-side evidence of what happened.
proposed_fix: Mirror the detach path: capture the result, ignore `DaemonError::NotFound` (an already-closed terminal is expected), and `tracing::warn!(%error, %terminal, "failed to resync a lagged client")` otherwise. Better, have `request_full_frames` return the set of terminals it could not resync so the caller can drop them from `attached` (forcing a clean re-attach) rather than silently serving diffs against an unknown grid.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test] async fn a_failed_lag_resync_is_reported()` in `server/connection.rs`'s test module, extending the existing `event_lag_forces_reconnect_and_full_frames` (connection.rs:1072-1216): after attaching, close the terminal host so `RequestFullFrame` returns a non-`NotFound` error, saturate the `BroadcastBus::new(1)` to force `RecvError::Lagged`, and assert with `tracing_test`'s captured subscriber that a `warn` naming the terminal was emitted (and/or that the terminal was removed from `attached`, observable through `services.sessions.attachment_count(terminal) == 0`). Today nothing is logged and the assertion fails.
verify_reason: The inconsistency is real and the harm is plausible. connection.rs:513-527 discards the dispatch result with `let _ignored`, while the disconnect path at connection.rs:343-357 classifies the identical call and warns on anything that is not `NotFound`. The error is reachable and not merely theoretical: the dispatch reaches `SessionsService::request_full_frame` -> `host_or_not_found(terminal)?.request_full()` (services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:119-123), and `TerminalHost` command submission can fail with `HostError::QueueFull` (fleet-term/src/host.rs:147, :373) under exactly the backlog that produced the lag. Two qualifications: `let _ignored` on a best-effort fallible call is an established idiom here (services/pool.rs:92/:134, jobs/manager.rs:672, services/repos.rs:111), so this is a consistency fix rather than a new class of bug; and the client is not entirely defenceless — fleet-client/src/terminal.rs:296-300 resets `received_full = false` and re-requests a full frame on its *own* receiver lag. That self-healing does not cover the case here, though: when the daemon's connection actor is the one that lapped, the client's receiver sees no gap at all, so the daemon-side resync really is the only recovery, and its failure is currently invisible.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs (request_full_frames and its two call sites at :281 and :303) plus the existing connection.rs test module around event_lag_forces_reconnect_and_full_frames.
corrected_fix: Take only the first half of the proposal: capture the result, ignore `DaemonError::NotFound` (a terminal closed between the attach bookkeeping and the resync is expected), and `tracing::warn!(%error, %terminal, "failed to resync a lagged client")` otherwise — mirroring connection.rs:343-357 exactly. Reject the second half: removing the terminal from `attached` on failure would silently desynchronise the daemon-side attachment (the attachment lease/count is owned by the dispatch of `DetachTerminal`, connection.rs:437-441 and :343-357), leaking an attachment and its keep-alive rather than forcing a clean re-attach. If a stronger recovery is wanted, dispatch a real `DetachTerminal` and let the client re-attach, not a bare set mutation.

rule: rust-ipc-protocol rule 11: link liveness is an explicit state a peer can observe, not something the peer infers from a closed socket
summary: `Listener::run` publishes `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` only after its loop breaks on the shutdown token, but every `Connection::run` breaks on that same token first, so no client ever receives the event on a SIGTERM/Ctrl-C shutdown.
failure_scenario: `fleetd` receives SIGTERM (systemd stop, `kill`, Ctrl-C in a foreground run) while the app is connected. Every connection actor takes its `shutdown.cancelled()` branch and stops draining `events`; the listener then publishes `DaemonShuttingDown` into a bus with no live readers. The app's client sees only a closed socket, so `fleet-client`'s `run_connection` treats it as a disconnect and reconnect-spins at the 2 s backoff cap forever instead of stopping, and `AppState` renders `fleetd connection lost` instead of the `fleetd stopped` banner that `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` drives (crates/fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:287-294; the wording contract is docs/UX-SPEC.md:1492). The graceful `DaemonShutdown` request path is only marginally better: the answering connection publishes the event and cancels the token in the same breath (server/connection.rs:254-255), so for every *other* connection both `shutdown.cancelled()` and `events.recv()` are ready and tokio picks at random.
proposed_fix: Publish the event before cancelling/breaking, not after: in `Listener::run`, subscribe the shutdown token to a small pre-cancel hook — e.g. move `self.events.publish(Event::DaemonShuttingDown)` to fire on the `shutdown.cancelled()` branch *before* `break`, and in `Connection::run` give the shutdown branch a short drain (`select!` biased to `events.recv()` for one pass, or check for a buffered `DaemonShuttingDown` and enqueue it) so the frame reaches the writer before the outbound channel is dropped.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test] async fn signal_shutdown_tells_connected_clients_the_daemon_stopped()` to `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs`: bind a `Listener` with a `CancellationToken`, connect a `Framed` client, complete Hello + `Subscribe { events: all }`, then `shutdown.cancel()` and read frames until EOF, asserting an `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` frame arrived. Today the stream reaches EOF without it.
verify_reason: Verified end to end. crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/listener.rs:184-212 publishes `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` only after the accept loop breaks, and the break is on the same `CancellationToken` (`() = self.shutdown.cancelled() => break Ok(())`) that every `Connection::run` breaks on (crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:141-142); main.rs:96-102 cancels that token from the signal handler, publishing nothing itself. So on SIGTERM/Ctrl-C the event lands in a bus whose readers have already left their select loops. The graceful path is a genuine race as described: connection.rs:254-255 publishes then cancels in the same breath, leaving other connections with two ready branches. No test covers delivery — `grep shutdown crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs` shows only `shutdown.cancel()` at :322 with no event assertion. The UX consequence is real: crates/fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:287-294 is the only producer of `DaemonLossReason::Stopped`, and shell/daemon.rs:61-62 maps it to `fleetd stopped` vs `fleetd connection lost`, while docs/UX-SPEC.md §3.12 case C ("Daemon died while attached") prescribes `fleetd stopped`. I do not accept the secondary claim that the client 'reconnect-spins forever instead of stopping' is itself a defect — reconnecting after an unannounced death is the designed behaviour (the app respawns fleetd); the defect is the missing announcement and the wrong banner.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs (shutdown branch), possibly listener.rs/main.rs, crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs (new test), crates/fleet-app/src/shell/daemon.rs banner expectations already exist; docs/UX-SPEC.md §3.12 wording table should be reconciled in the same commit.
corrected_fix: Do not rely on the bus at all for this — the proposal's 'publish before break, plus a biased drain' still races, because the listener does not own the cancellation (main.rs does) and a biased select cannot prove the event was already published. Instead make it deterministic per connection: in `Connection::run`'s `() = self.shutdown.cancelled()` branch, before breaking, `enqueue_event(&outbound, Event::DaemonShuttingDown)` when `subscriptions` contains that kind (bounded by the existing SOCKET_WRITE_TIMEOUT path that already drains the writer at connection.rs:317-336). Keep the listener publish for in-process subscribers, and leave connection.rs:254 alone — the requesting client already learns from `ResponseBody::ShuttingDown` (crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:482).

rule: rust-ipc-protocol rule 3 (deadline on every wire await) and rule 4 (bounded admission) — the admission permit is released only when this task ends
summary: The disconnect cleanup loop dispatches one `DetachTerminal` per attached terminal with no deadline; for a remote terminal that call goes over `RemoteEndpoint::request`, which has no deadline either, so a client disconnect can hold its `MAX_CONNECTIONS` admission permit forever.
failure_scenario: A host link is `Ready` but its writer is blocked (see ipc-link-write-unbounded) or the remote is applying reader backpressure. The app quits, so its socket closes and `Connection::run` leaves the loop with one remote terminal in `attached`. The cleanup `DetachTerminal` is enqueued to the link and never answered, so the connection task never returns and its semaphore permit is never released. Each app restart repeats it; after 128 such disconnects `try_admit` returns `None` and the daemon rejects every new client with `rejecting client above connection limit` while looking otherwise healthy.
proposed_fix: Bound the cleanup: wrap the loop (or each dispatch) in `tokio::time::timeout(SOCKET_WRITE_TIMEOUT, …)` — the constant already exists at connection.rs:34 — and log a warning on expiry rather than waiting. Independently, give `RemoteEndpoint::request` a deadline so no daemon-internal caller can block forever on a remote hop.
test_plan: Add a test to `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_lifecycle.rs`: install a `FakeRemote` endpoint whose `state()` is `Ready` and whose `request()` future never resolves, attach a remote terminal over a real socket `Connection`, then drop the client socket and assert `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), connection_task).await.is_ok()`. Today the task is still running when the timeout fires.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:341-358: the post-loop cleanup awaits `dispatch_routed_with_owner(DetachTerminal { .. })` per attached terminal with no deadline, after the writer has already been joined/aborted, and the admission permit is held for the whole task (listener.rs:198-203 `let _permit = permit;`, MAX_CONNECTIONS = 128 at listener.rs:29). For a remote terminal that dispatch reaches Router::forward (router/mod.rs:134-168), which only short-circuits when `endpoint.state() == LinkState::Down`; a Ready-but-wedged link then hits `RemoteLink::request` (link.rs:280-304), whose two selects race only `states.changed()` — no deadline anywhere on that path, and no timeout in services/router (grep shows timeouts only in sessions.rs/create.rs). `attached` really can hold remote ids (run_terminal_request at connection.rs:428-476 inserts on any successful AttachTerminal, routed or not). The precondition (a Ready link that never answers) is exactly ipc-link-write-unbounded, so this is a compounding defect rather than an independent one, but the missing deadline is directly in the code.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs (cleanup loop) plus a test in crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_lifecycle.rs and a fake endpoint in crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/. If the second half of the proposal were taken it would additionally touch machines/link.rs, router/mod.rs and every long-running remote request path.
corrected_fix: Bound the cleanup loop only: wrap the whole `for terminal in attached` loop in one `tokio::time::timeout(SOCKET_WRITE_TIMEOUT, ...)` (connection.rs:34) and warn on expiry, so the permit is always released. Reject the proposal's second half — do **not** give `RemoteEndpoint::request` a blanket deadline. Remote CreateWorktree/clone/board calls legitimately run for minutes and the client already exempts them by name (crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:678-700 `request_timeout`); a blanket link deadline would turn those into spurious transport errors while the remote keeps doing the work. The correct systemic fix for the underlying hang is the write budget in ipc-link-write-unbounded, which flips the link to Down and fails pending, at which point `forward`'s existing Down check answers instantly.

rule: rust-ipc-protocol rule 1 / checklist 8: one connection-state model, and the client's replayed subscription must reproduce what the daemon actually holds
summary: The daemon *adds* to a connection's subscription set on `Subscribe`, while the client API documents and models it as a *replace*, so the two sides disagree about what a connection is subscribed to and a reconnect silently changes the delivered event set.
evidence:
Daemon, crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:171-174:
```rust
RequestBody::Subscribe { events } => {
    subscriptions.extend(events);
    Some(Ok(ResponseBody::Ack))
}
```
Client API, crates/fleet-client/src/api/daemon.rs:36-42:
```rust
/// Replaces this connection's event subscriptions.
pub async fn subscribe(&self, events: Vec<EventKind>) -> Result<()> {
```
Client connection state, crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:573:
```rust
Self::Subscribe(events) => state.subscriptions = events,
```
and the reconnect handshake replays exactly that field (connection.rs:711-722). `docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:509` ("Explicit subscriptions should include all four kinds") reads as replace semantics too.
failure_scenario: A caller does `client.subscribe(vec![TerminalFrame])` and later `client.subscribe(vec![JobUpdated])`. Per the documented contract it should now receive only `JobUpdated`; it keeps receiving `TerminalFrame` because the daemon holds the union. Then the daemon restarts or the socket drops: `establish` re-subscribes with `state.subscriptions`, which is only `[JobUpdated]`, and `TerminalFrame` stops arriving. The same connection therefore delivers two different event sets before and after a reconnect, with nothing in either log saying so. (The union semantics are load-bearing today for `Mirror::refresh`, crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mirror.rs:394-399, which issues a second, narrower `Subscribe` on a link already subscribed to all kinds by `establish_before` — so whichever side is changed, that caller must change with it.)
proposed_fix: Pick one and make both sides and the doc agree. Replace is the safer contract given the client's reconnect replay: change the daemon to `subscriptions = events.into_iter().collect()`, and change `Mirror::refresh` to request the full kind set it needs (or drop its redundant `Subscribe` entirely, since `establish_before` already subscribed to all 16 kinds). Add a golden/legacy-peer note if you instead keep `extend`, and fix the rustdoc on `Client::subscribe` plus `ConnectionEffect::Subscribe` to accumulate.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test] async fn a_second_subscribe_replaces_the_first()` in `crates/fleet-client/tests/client.rs`: against the scripted daemon, subscribe to `[EventKind::JobUpdated]` after connect, have the daemon publish an `Event::Toast`, and assert the client receives nothing. Pair it with a daemon-side test in `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs` that sends `Subscribe { [Toast] }` then `Subscribe { [JobUpdated] }` and asserts a published `Event::Toast` is not written to that socket. Both fail today.
verify_reason: The divergence is real and I read both halves: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:171-174 does `subscriptions.extend(events)`, while crates/fleet-client/src/api/daemon.rs:36 documents 'Replaces this connection's event subscriptions' and crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:573 models it as `state.subscriptions = events`, replayed verbatim on reconnect (connection.rs:711-722). But the described failure cannot occur today: nothing in production calls `Client::subscribe` — the only callers are crates/fleet-app/tests/common/mod.rs:70 and crates/fleet-client/tests/client.rs:285, and `ConnectionState::default` already subscribes to all 18 kinds (connection.rs:136, `all_event_kinds`). So this is a latent rustdoc/model mismatch, not a live bug, and docs/ says nothing either way (fleet-proto/src/request.rs:352 'Subscribe this connection to event families' is neutral; docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:509 is about which kinds to include, not about replace semantics).
blast_radius: With my correction: crates/fleet-client/src/api/daemon.rs rustdoc, the `ConnectionEffect::Subscribe` apply arm in crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:573, one line in docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md §Subscribe. With the finding's own fix it would instead touch crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs, crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mirror.rs, crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_mirror.rs and every remote terminal/agent test.
corrected_fix: Make the client match the daemon, not the reverse. Changing the daemon to `subscriptions = events.into_iter().collect()` would break remote machines outright: `establish_before` subscribes the link to all kinds (link.rs:611-616) and `Mirror::refresh` (mirror.rs:392-400) then issues a narrower `Subscribe { SnapshotChanged, SessionChanged, AgentSummary }` on that same connection — under replace semantics the local daemon would stop receiving remote `TerminalFrame`, `TerminalExited`, `HostLinkChanged` and agent events, killing remote terminal streaming. So: fix the rustdoc on `Client::subscribe` to say it adds kinds, make `ConnectionEffect::Subscribe` union into `state.subscriptions` (dedup) so the reconnect replay reproduces the daemon's real set, keep `Unsubscribe` as the clear-all, and state the additive rule once in docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage: "a test that cannot fail is a deleted test with extra steps"; "Is the test named as a sentence stating the invariant?"
summary: `nearly_expired_command_retains_connection_write_budget` builds no command and asserts a relation between two compile-time constants, so it can never fail and never touches the code path its name describes.
failure_scenario: The assertion expands to `t2 + 10s > t1 + 1ms + 5s` where `t1 <= t2` are two successive `Instant::now()` readings — true for any pair of readings, for any command, forever. Concretely: change `send_command` to clamp the socket write deadline to `command.expires_at` (the exact regression the name forbids, which would make a nearly-expired request tear down the connection instead of being written) and this test still passes, because it never constructs a `Command` and never calls `send_command`.
proposed_fix: Assert the real invariant on the real path: build a `Command` with `expires_at: Some(Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1))`, drive `send_command` against a `tokio::io::duplex` peer that never reads, and assert the write is attempted (and the request only fails with the "timed out" text) rather than the connection being dropped. If only the constant relation matters, make it a `const` assertion: `const _: () = assert!(WRITE_BUDGET.as_millis() > REQUEST_TIMEOUT.as_millis() / 2);` and delete the runtime test.
test_plan: Add `a_request_one_millisecond_from_expiry_is_still_written_to_the_socket`: create the oneshot-backed `Command` with `expires_at = now + 1ms`, run `send_command` over `tokio::io::duplex(64)`, assert the encoded frame appears on the peer half. Then patch `socket_write_deadline` to `Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1)` — the new test fails, while `nearly_expired_command_retains_connection_write_budget` keeps passing, proving the old one is inert.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:1065-1071 builds no Command and calls nothing on the dispatch path. `socket_write_deadline()` (:455-457) is `Instant::now() + WRITE_BUDGET` and takes no arguments, so the assertion reduces to `t2 + 10s > t1 + 1ms + 5s` for two successive monotonic readings with t1 <= t2 — true unconditionally. `send_command` (:395-451) computes the deadline from `socket_write_deadline()` alone and never consults `command.expires_at` after `command_for_dispatch`, so the named invariant is real but wholly unexercised by this test.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs `mod tests` only (needs `Framed::split` types `TransportWriter`/`TransportReader`, both already in the module). No production code, no other crate.
corrected_fix: Delete the tautology. Replace it with a `#[tokio::test]` on the real path: build `Command { request: Request { id: 1, body: RequestBody::DaemonPing }, response: Some(tx), expires_at: Some(Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1)) }`, split a `protocol_transport` over `tokio::io::duplex(1024)` into `TransportWriter`/`TransportReader`, call `send_command(...)` and assert it returns `DispatchOutcome::Sent` (the peer half stays alive but unread; a 64-byte frame fits the duplex buffer). Do NOT use the proposed `const _: () = assert!(WRITE_BUDGET.as_millis() > REQUEST_TIMEOUT.as_millis() / 2)`: that constant relation is not the invariant (the risk is per-command clamping, not budget sizing) and `Duration::as_millis` in a const item is a needless portability bet. Note the deadline is `tokio::time::Instant`, so the replacement must be a tokio test, unlike the current plain `#[test]`.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage: "Does a non-trivial change ship with a test?" — untested branches on reconnect are the skill's named risk area ("error paths, reconnect, cancellation")
summary: The reconnect queue's two most delicate branches — dropping a superseded `ResizeTerminal` for the same terminal, and expiring queued commands with the "timed out while reconnecting" message — have no test at all, although both are plain functions in the same module as `mod tests`.
failure_scenario: Drop the `queued.response.is_none()` guard on the *queued* side of the `position` predicate and the coalescer will delete a resize that someone is awaiting a reply for; that caller's `oneshot` is dropped, so its `request()` resolves to a bare `RecvError` instead of the transport error the rest of the code produces — and no test notices. Equally, widen the predicate to ignore `terminal` and a two-pane window loses one pane's resize across every reconnect, leaving a permanently mis-sized PTY.
proposed_fix: None needed in production code; add the unit tests. Both functions take plain `&mut VecDeque<Command>` and need no runtime.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs`'s `mod tests`: (1) `a_queued_resize_is_superseded_only_for_the_same_terminal` — push fire-and-forget `ResizeTerminal{terminal: TerminalId(1), 80x24}`, then `TerminalId(2)`, then `TerminalId(1), 100x40`; assert the queue is `[t2, t1@100x40]`. (2) `an_awaited_resize_is_never_dropped_by_coalescing` — push a resize carrying a `response` sender, then a fire-and-forget resize for the same terminal; assert both are queued and the sender is still open. (3) `discard_obsolete_commands_fails_expired_entries_with_the_reconnecting_message` — queue one command with `expires_at` in the past and assert its receiver yields a `ProtoError` whose message contains "while reconnecting". All three fail against the mutations above.
verify_reason: Verified untested and verified live. `grep -rn 'queue_disconnected_command|discard_obsolete_commands' crates/fleet-client` hits only the definitions (connection.rs:652,675) and their two internal call sites (:627,:621/:646); no test in src or tests/ names either, and tests/bugfix_connection.rs:285-317 only proves channel backpressure. The coalescer is not dead code: the app sends resizes fire-and-forget through `Bridge::send` (fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/lifecycle.rs:129, workspace/terminal.rs:66, agent_popup/terminal.rs:47), which reaches `send_background` (connection.rs:264-271) with `response: None` — exactly the branch the predicate keys on. `api/terminals.rs:142` is the awaited path the `response.is_none()` guard is there to protect.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs `mod tests` only — both functions take `&mut VecDeque<Command>`, need no runtime, and `Command`/`RequestBody::ResizeTerminal`/`oneshot` are already in scope there.
corrected_fix: Fix as proposed (tests only, no production change), with one refinement to the third case: `discard_obsolete_commands` expires entries only when a reconnect *attempt fails* (:646) or on entry to the disconnected loop (:621), so name the test for that trigger and drive the plain function directly rather than implying the message appears on every reconnect. Assert the receiver yields a `ProtoError` whose message contains 'while reconnecting' via `try_recv` after `fail_command` runs synchronously.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage/Real processes: a real-daemon test must "prove a genuinely cross-process concern"; a branch that swallows its own assertion proves nothing
summary: `a_shutdown_reads_as_a_lost_daemon_not_as_a_crash` makes its `DaemonShuttingDown` observation optional — if the event never arrives it falls through to a ping-failure loop that passes — so no test in the workspace verifies that the daemon actually publishes `Event::DaemonShuttingDown`.
failure_scenario: Delete `self.events.publish(Event::DaemonShuttingDown);` at `server/connection.rs:254`. Every test still passes: this one takes the `!saw_shutdown` branch and the ping loop still errors once the process exits. In the app, `state/connection.rs:288` never runs, so the shell shows the generic reconnect-backoff path instead of `DaemonLink::Lost`, and the user sees "reconnecting…" spinners after an explicit `fleet daemon stop`.
proposed_fix: Split the concerns: keep the socket-loss assertion here, and add a daemon-side in-process test that drives `Connection` over `tokio::io::duplex` through a `DaemonShutdown` request and asserts the bus published `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` before the connection closed — no race with process teardown, so the assertion can be unconditional.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs`, add `an_explicit_shutdown_publishes_daemon_shutting_down_before_the_socket_closes`: subscribe to the `BroadcastBus`, drive a `Connection` over `tokio::io::duplex` with `RequestBody::DaemonShutdown`, and assert the next event on the bus is `Event::DaemonShuttingDown`. Removing the publish at `server/connection.rs:254` makes it fail; today it makes nothing fail.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/tests/jobs_panel.rs:225-252 is exactly as quoted: `.unwrap_or(false)` on the timeout, then an `if !saw_shutdown` ping loop that passes as soon as the process stops answering. `grep -rn DaemonShuttingDown crates/fleet-daemon/tests` returns nothing, and the only positive assertion on the event (crates/fleet-client/tests/client.rs:319-326) comes from a hand-scripted server, not from the daemon. So deleting the publish at server/connection.rs:254 (or listener.rs:212) leaves the whole workspace green while fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:288 stops firing. The optional branch itself is a defensible race guard — the gap is that nothing else covers the publish.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs only (reuses its `services(&home)` helper at :341 and the Listener/Framed fixture at :214). fleet-app/tests/jobs_panel.rs unchanged; no production code.
corrected_fix: Keep jobs_panel.rs as is (its comment documents a genuine flush/teardown race). Add the daemon-side test, but not as proposed: `Connection::new` (server/connection.rs:57-65) takes a concrete `UnixStream`, so `tokio::io::duplex` will not compile. Follow the existing pattern at crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs:214-240 — bind a real `Listener`, connect a `Framed<UnixStream, FleetCodec<Request, Value>>` client, subscribe to the `BroadcastBus` first, send `RequestBody::DaemonShutdown`, and assert `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` arrives on the bus. Also assert it is published only after the response is enqueued (connection.rs:248-256 orders it that way deliberately), otherwise the test locks in nothing about ordering.
